title: SOLAIR user manual
subtitle: A practical guide for drivers and TODA users
introduction: Use SOLAIR to review your assigned e-trike, recorded location, energy readings, alerts and assistance requests. This guide follows the current app menus. Available controls depend on your account role and assignments.

sections.title: Get started and sign in
sections.summary: Create your account, sign in and confirm the workspace you are using.

steps.title: Open SOLAIR
steps.text: On a phone, select Get started on the welcome screen. On a laptop, use the sign-in page. You can keep using the app in a supported browser.

steps.title: Create an account if needed
steps.text: Choose Sign up. Enter your account details, requested role, vehicle type where shown, matching passwords and Philippine mobile number. Follow any email-confirmation instructions before signing in.

steps.title: Sign in
steps.text: Enter your email and password. Account creation does not automatically assign an existing vehicle or grant operator permissions.

steps.title: Choose notification badges
steps.text: New accounts see a one-time introduction. Get notified enables in-app notifications; Later keeps the current preference. You can change it in Settings.

steps.title: Review your workspace
steps.text: Check the TODA name and selected vehicle. If assignments are incomplete, use Review setup or open Registration. Ask your TODA administrator to link the correct account, vehicle and responsible operator.

notes.title: Hardware and demonstration modes
notes.text: Real hardware uses reported device records. Demonstration data is simulated. Check the mode label before interpreting a reading or exporting a file.

notes.title: Refresh and sign out
notes.text: Refresh keeps the current page. Use Log out in the hamburger menu or account menu when finished on a shared device.

sections.title: Home and Registration
sections.summary: Find your assigned vehicle and understand the main dashboard cards.

steps.title: Review My vehicle / Home
steps.text: The assigned-vehicle card shows your model and TODA. Energy at a glance contains battery voltage/current, solar harvested energy, wind harvested energy and solar power.

steps.title: Read vehicle status
steps.text: Device connection, Battery, Location and Security report different conditions. A recent device connection does not mean every sensor reading is current.

steps.title: Use quick actions
steps.text: Find my vehicle opens Location, Check my alerts opens Alerts, and Ask my TODA for help opens the assistance area.

steps.title: Open Registration
steps.text: Open the hamburger menu and choose Registration, directly above Help. The same details are available through Settings > My registration and assignments.

steps.title: Review and update your details
steps.text: Check your TODA, vehicle ID/model and responsible operator. You may update your declared vehicle type and GPS/map display name, then choose Save registration details. Assignment changes require an administrator.

notes.title: Unknown values
notes.text: A dash, No data, Not available or State unknown means a usable reading is unavailable. Treat old or uncalibrated readings according to their label.

notes.title: Battery information
notes.text: Voltage is not a remaining-battery percentage or driving range. Battery current is signed: positive indicates charging and negative indicates discharging when correctly calibrated.

sections.title: Location and recorded journeys
sections.summary: Use reported GPS positions, the recorded track and detected stops.

steps.title: Open Location
steps.text: Use the Location bottom tab or hamburger item. A vehicle marker needs valid reported GPS coordinates. Manila, Malabon or Metro Manila can appear as a reference when there is no valid fix.

steps.title: Review the selected vehicle
steps.text: Use its marker or the vehicle selector where available. Open selected vehicle shows its details. Refresh requests updated records.

steps.title: View a recorded track
steps.text: When GPS history exists, use Show recorded track and Fit track. The blue path represents recorded sections; endpoint markers identify the beginning and latest recorded point.

steps.title: Review Location History
steps.text: Choose a minimum stop duration of 1, 2, 5 or 10 minutes. A possible stop requires at least three valid reports within 60 m of the first fix for the selected duration. Select a stop to focus it on the map.

steps.title: Check time and distance
steps.text: First and last recorded times use Asia/Manila (UTC+8). Distances between stops sum valid recorded GPS segments and are estimates. Return to vehicle location clears the historical-stop focus.

notes.title: A city reference is not a vehicle position
notes.text: No valid GPS positions means a device fix is still needed. A last known position may be old.

notes.title: Addresses and track gaps
notes.text: Street addresses currently show Address unavailable until address lookup is connected. Missing fixes, gaps over five minutes and implausible jumps break the track; the app does not invent a connecting route.

sections.title: Energy readings and line graphs
sections.summary: Read battery, solar and wind measurements with their units and data quality.

steps.title: Open Energy
steps.text: Select Energy. Use the Solar and Wind links to move to their sections. The illustrations identify energy sources; they do not confirm installed hardware or commissioning.

steps.title: Read solar measurements
steps.text: Solar cards show PV input voltage (V), PV input current (A), PV power (W) and controller output (V / A). Recorded solar harvest is shown in watt-hours (Wh).

steps.title: Read wind measurements
steps.text: Wind cards show output voltage (V), output current (A), power (W) and energy yield (Wh). A Not commissioned label remains until commissioning has been established.

steps.title: Use the line graphs
steps.text: Graphs appear when valid timestamped readings are available. Home includes four energy trends and a battery-voltage trend in vehicle status. Energy shows the individual electrical channels.

steps.title: Interpret gaps and totals
steps.text: Graphs use up to 24 samples. Missing values and gaps over 30 seconds are not joined. One sample is a point, not a trend. Wh charts describe energy in the displayed sample window; card totals can cover a longer recorded period.

notes.title: Calibration and old readings
notes.text: Uncalibrated hardware electrical values are withheld. Old reading, Time unknown and Calibration needed describe the available evidence; they are not fresh measurements.

notes.title: Mobile and laptop layouts
notes.text: On mobile, value cards can rise over the illustration while scrolling. Laptop images stay above their cards. Both layouts show the same recorded data.

sections.title: Alerts and Notifications
sections.summary: Review reported security activity and manage in-app notification badges.

steps.title: Open Alerts
steps.text: Choose Alerts to review reported security events for the selected vehicle and data mode. Device and sensor freshness affect whether a state can be interpreted.

steps.title: Review recorded handling
steps.text: Authorized TODA personnel can acknowledge incidents and record follow-up where their role permits. Drivers can review available handling details.

steps.title: Open Notifications
steps.text: Use the Notifications bottom tab. Choose a category to filter activity, open an update to view its related page, or use Mark all read.

steps.title: Manage notification preferences
steps.text: Open the notification settings icon or Settings > Notifications. Save the in-app badge preference. Recorded activity remains accessible when badges are off.

steps.title: Find earlier records
steps.text: Use View history & reports from Notifications, or History & Reports in the hamburger menu, to review available saved data.

notes.title: Reading does not acknowledge an incident
notes.text: Marking a notification as read changes its read marker. It does not acknowledge or resolve a security incident.

notes.title: In-app updates, push and SMS
notes.text: In-app badge preferences do not enable browser push. SMS contact, verification and sending configuration are managed separately; saving a preference is not proof of message delivery.

sections.title: Help and assistance requests
sections.summary: Find a quick answer, read this manual or request help from your TODA.

steps.title: Search the help center
steps.text: Open Help from the hamburger menu. Type a topic in Search help, then expand an FAQ question to read its answer. Clear the search to show all topics.

steps.title: Open or save this manual
steps.text: Select User manual. Read the guide in the popup, use its section links, or choose Download PDF to save a copy. Use the close button or Escape to return to Help.

steps.title: Prepare an assistance request
steps.text: On the assistance page, choose an assistance type and describe what happened and how your operator can reach you. The request concerns the selected assigned vehicle.

steps.title: Send and verify receipt
steps.text: Select Send help request once. Server received means the server accepted it and operator acknowledgment is still pending. QUEUED / UNSENT means server receipt has not been confirmed.

steps.title: Check Request activity
steps.text: Review request status and recorded operator follow-up. A pending request is not an acknowledgment. If offline requests remain queued, reconnect and use Retry delivery.

steps.title: Use the right follow-up
steps.text: Use Send a message for the existing TODA conversation where you have an assigned vehicle. Report a problem records an app issue for your administrator; do not include passwords or device tokens.

notes.title: Assistance delivery
notes.text: SOLAIR requests go through the configured TODA workflow. The app does not confirm that outside emergency services have been contacted.

notes.title: Keyboard use
notes.text: Tab and Shift+Tab move between controls. Enter or Space activates buttons. Escape closes the manual popup and supported menus.

sections.title: Settings and your profile
sections.summary: Use individual settings pages for your account, photo and preferences.

steps.title: Open Settings
steps.text: Select Settings to see your profile summary and grouped Account details, General and Support options. Each detail page has Back to settings.

steps.title: Edit your account name
steps.text: Choose Edit profile or Account profile, update Name and choose Save profile. Email is read-only here; use Contact & SMS preferences for a verified email change.

steps.title: Add a profile photo
steps.text: Choose profile photo, select a .png or readable .img file up to 3 MB, check the preview and choose Save photo. Replace it by choosing another file, or use Remove photo to restore your initials.

steps.title: Manage contact preferences
steps.text: Open Contact & SMS preferences to update your mobile number or optional SMS consent. Changing a number removes its verification. Verification controls depend on the configured service.

steps.title: Choose an appearance
steps.text: Open Light / Dark mode and choose Light, Dark or System. System follows your device. Your selection persists after refresh.

steps.title: Review support and policies
steps.text: Settings includes Help and support, Report a problem, Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Policy pages are marked as drafts for review.

notes.title: Your photo stays with your account
notes.text: A saved photo appears in Settings, the account menu and sidebar. Initials remain when no photo is saved.

notes.title: Review assignments separately
notes.text: My registration and assignments is an individual page. A profile edit or photo upload does not change your TODA, vehicle assignment or role.

sections.title: Reports and quick troubleshooting
sections.summary: Export available records and check common no-data situations.

steps.title: Open History & Reports
steps.text: Use the hamburger menu. The Research evidence card offers research CSV, CPE readings CSV and, in hardware mode, incident evidence CSV. Bench exports are role-dependent.

steps.title: Review the archive
steps.text: The telemetry archive provides available saved rows and JSON export. Always check the selected vehicle and data mode before downloading.

steps.title: Understand export limits
steps.text: Telemetry and CPE exports include up to the newest 5,000 rows; incident exports include up to the newest 200 records with available handling and delivery information. Unknown times remain blank.

steps.title: If readings or a graph are empty
steps.text: Check the assigned vehicle, hardware/demo label, device contact and calibration status. Empty charts are expected when usable history is missing. Use the shown retry control if a history request fails.

steps.title: If a location or request is missing
steps.text: A GPS reference map needs a valid device fix before it can show the vehicle. For requests, check whether the state says server received or QUEUED / UNSENT, then check for operator acknowledgment.

steps.title: If access is incomplete
steps.text: Open Account setup and Registration. Ask the TODA administrator to confirm membership, the assigned vehicle, responsible operator and any requested operator role. Refresh after the change is confirmed.

notes.title: Saved evidence has limits
notes.text: Exporting a file does not establish physical acceptance, calibration or successful message delivery. Use the source and quality labels included with the records.

notes.title: Keep your account secure
notes.text: Do not include passwords, device tokens or private credentials in messages or bug reports. Sign out when using a shared device.
